8	# Stalks and specializations on a scheme with Dedekind section rings
9	
10	A scheme covered by affine opens whose section rings are Dedekind domains behaves like a
11	smooth curve: its stalks are valuation rings (fields at generic points, DVRs at closed
12	points), and its specialization order has height one.  This file proves the pointwise
13	statements from the single hypothesis "`x` lies in an affine open with Dedekind section
14	ring", and derives the two consumers needed for the finite-fibers argument of the map to
15	`ℙ¹`:
16	
17	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineOpen.valuationRing_stalk`: the stalk at a point of an affine
18	  open with Dedekind section ring is a valuation ring.
19	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineOpen.specializes_eq_genericPoint_or_eq`: on an irreducible
20	  scheme, a generalization of such a point is the generic point or the point itself.
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.finite_of_isClosed_of_notMem_genericPoint`: on an irreducible,
22	  Noetherian scheme all of whose points have only trivial generalizations, a closed subset
23	  avoiding the generic point is finite.
24	
25	Finally the hypotheses are discharged for a scheme smooth of relative dimension one over a
26	field, using the standard smooth charts and
27	`Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.isDedekindDomain`:

46	/-- The stalk of an integral scheme at a point of an affine open whose section ring is a
47	Dedekind domain is a valuation ring: the localization of a Dedekind domain at a prime is a
48	field (at `⊥`) or a discrete valuation ring (at a maximal ideal), and both are valuation
49	rings. -/
50	theorem IsAffineOpen.valuationRing_stalk [IsIntegral X] {V : X.Opens} (hV : IsAffineOpen V)
51	    (hD : IsDedekindDomain Γ(X, V)) {x : X} (hx : x ∈ V) :
52	    ValuationRing (X.presheaf.stalk x) := by
53	  letI : Algebra Γ(X, V) (X.presheaf.stalk x) := X.presheaf.algebra_section_stalk ⟨x, hx⟩
54	  have hloc : IsLocalization.AtPrime (X.presheaf.stalk x) (hV.primeIdealOf ⟨x, hx⟩).asIdeal :=
55	    hV.isLocalization_stalk ⟨x, hx⟩
56	  set q := hV.primeIdealOf ⟨x, hx⟩ with hq
57	  by_cases hbot : q.asIdeal = ⊥
58	  · -- At the generic point of `V` the stalk is the fraction field.
59	    have hsub : q.asIdeal.primeCompl = nonZeroDivisors Γ(X, V) := by
60	      ext z
61	      simp [Ideal.primeCompl, hbot, mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff_ne_zero]
62	    have hfrac : IsLocalization (nonZeroDivisors Γ(X, V)) (X.presheaf.stalk x) := by
63	      rw [← hsub]
64	      exact hloc
65	    letI : Field (X.presheaf.stalk x) := IsFractionRing.toField Γ(X, V)
66	    infer_instance
67	  · -- At other points the stalk is a DVR.
68	    have : IsDiscreteValuationRing (X.presheaf.stalk x) :=
69	      IsLocalization.AtPrime.isDiscreteValuationRing_of_dedekind_domain Γ(X, V) hbot _
70	    infer_instance

72	/-- On an irreducible scheme, a generalization of a point of an affine open with Dedekind
73	section ring is the generic point or the point itself: primes of a Dedekind domain below a
74	given prime are `⊥` or the prime itself. -/
75	theorem IsAffineOpen.specializes_eq_genericPoint_or_eq [IrreducibleSpace X] {V : X.Opens}
76	    (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (hD : IsDedekindDomain Γ(X, V)) {x y : X} (hx : x ∈ V)
77	    (h : y ⤳ x) : y = genericPoint X ∨ y = x := by
78	  have hy : y ∈ V := h.mem_open V.2 hx
79	  set py := hV.primeIdealOf ⟨y, hy⟩ with hpy
80	  set px := hV.primeIdealOf ⟨x, hx⟩ with hpx
81	  have hyx : hV.fromSpec.base py = y := hV.fromSpec_primeIdealOf ⟨y, hy⟩
82	  have hxx : hV.fromSpec.base px = x := hV.fromSpec_primeIdealOf ⟨x, hx⟩
83	  -- Transfer the specialization along the open immersion `Spec Γ(X, V) ⟶ X`.
84	  have hspec : py ⤳ px := by
85	    refine hV.fromSpec.isOpenEmbedding.isInducing.specializes_iff.mp ?_
86	    rw [hyx, hxx]
87	    exact h
88	  have hle : py.asIdeal ≤ px.asIdeal := (PrimeSpectrum.le_iff_specializes py px).mpr hspec
89	  by_cases hbot : py.asIdeal = ⊥
90	  · -- `y` is the image of the generic point of `Spec Γ(X, V)`.
91	    left
92	    have hgen : (genericPoint (Spec Γ(X, V)) : Spec Γ(X, V)) = py := by
93	      rw [genericPoint_eq_bot_of_affine]
94	      exact (PrimeSpectrum.ext hbot).symm
95	    rw [← hyx, ← hgen, genericPoint_eq_of_isOpenImmersion hV.fromSpec]
96	  · -- A nonzero prime of a Dedekind domain is maximal, so `py = px`.
97	    right
98	    have hmax : py.asIdeal.IsMaximal := py.isPrime.isMaximal hbot
99	    have : py.asIdeal = px.asIdeal := hmax.eq_of_le px.isPrime.ne_top hle
100	    rw [← hyx, ← hxx, PrimeSpectrum.ext this]
101	
102	end Pointwise

106	/-- On an irreducible scheme whose specialization order has height one (every strict
107	generalization is the generic point), every non-generic point is closed. -/
108	theorem Scheme.isClosed_singleton_of_forall_specializes [IrreducibleSpace X]
109	    (hgen : ∀ x y : X, y ⤳ x → y = genericPoint X ∨ y = x) {x : X}
110	    (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) : IsClosed ({x} : Set X) := by
111	  have : closure ({x} : Set X) ⊆ {x} := by
112	    intro y hy
113	    have hxy : x ⤳ y := specializes_iff_mem_closure.mpr hy
114	    rcases hgen y x hxy with h | h
115	    · exact absurd h hx
116	    · exact h ▸ rfl
117	  exact closure_subset_iff_isClosed.mp this
118	
119	/-- **Finiteness of proper closed subsets of a curve-like scheme.**  On an irreducible,
120	Noetherian (as a topological space), sober scheme whose specialization order has height one,
121	a closed subset avoiding the generic point is finite: it is a finite union of irreducible
122	closed subsets, and each of these is the closure of a non-generic point, hence a singleton. -/
123	theorem Scheme.finite_of_isClosed_of_notMem_genericPoint [IrreducibleSpace X]
124	    [TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace X]
125	    (hgen : ∀ x y : X, y ⤳ x → y = genericPoint X ∨ y = x) {Z : Set X} (hZ : IsClosed Z)
126	    (hξ : genericPoint X ∉ Z) : Z.Finite := by
127	  obtain ⟨S, hSfin, hScl, hSirr, hSsup⟩ :=
128	    TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace.exists_finite_set_isClosed_irreducible hZ
129	  rw [hSsup]
130	  refine Set.Finite.sUnion hSfin fun t ht => ?_
131	  -- Each irreducible component of `Z` is the closure of a non-generic point, hence a
132	  -- singleton.
133	  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := QuasiSober.sober (hSirr t ht) (hScl t ht)
134	  have hzZ : z ∈ Z := hSsup ▸ Set.mem_sUnion.mpr ⟨t, ht, hz.mem⟩
135	  have hzξ : z ≠ genericPoint X := fun h => hξ (h ▸ hzZ)
136	  have hcl : IsClosed ({z} : Set X) :=
137	    Scheme.isClosed_singleton_of_forall_specializes hgen hzξ
138	  have : t = {z} := by
139	    rw [← hz.def, hcl.closure_eq]
140	  rw [this]
141	  exact Set.finite_singleton z
142	
143	end Finiteness

149	/-- Every point of an integral scheme smooth of relative dimension `1` over a field lies in
150	an affine open whose section ring is a Dedekind domain: a standard smooth chart of relative
151	dimension `1`. -/
152	theorem SmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_isDedekindDomain_section
153	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f] [IsIntegral X] (x : X) :
154	    ∃ V : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen V ∧ x ∈ V ∧ IsDedekindDomain Γ(X, V) := by
155	  obtain ⟨U, hU, V, hV, hxV, e, hsm⟩ :=
156	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_isStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension (n := 1) (f := f) x
157	  -- The base affine open is nonempty, hence is all of the one-point space `Spec K`.
158	  have hUtop : U = ⊤ := by
159	    have hsub : Subsingleton (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) :=
160	      inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (PrimeSpectrum K))
161	    refine TopologicalSpace.Opens.ext (Set.eq_univ_of_forall fun y => ?_)
162	    exact Subsingleton.elim (f.base x) y ▸ e hxV
163	  subst hUtop
164	  letI : Field Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of K), ⊤) :=
165	    ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv.toMulEquiv.isField
166	      (Field.toIsField K)).toField
167	  haveI : Nonempty V := ⟨⟨x, hxV⟩⟩
168	  algebraize [(f.appLE ⊤ V e).hom]
169	  exact ⟨V, hV, hxV, Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.isDedekindDomain
170	    Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of K), ⊤) Γ(X, V)⟩

172	/-- The stalks of an integral scheme smooth of relative dimension `1` over a field are
173	valuation rings. -/

175	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f] [IsIntegral X] (x : X) :
176	    ValuationRing (X.presheaf.stalk x) := by
177	  obtain ⟨V, hV, hxV, hD⟩ :=
178	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_isDedekindDomain_section f x
179	  exact hV.valuationRing_stalk hD hxV

181	/-- On an integral scheme smooth of relative dimension `1` over a field, the only
182	generalizations of a point are the generic point and the point itself. -/
183	theorem SmoothOfRelativeDimension.specializes_eq_genericPoint_or_eq
184	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f] [IsIntegral X] {x y : X} (h : y ⤳ x) :
185	    y = genericPoint X ∨ y = x := by
186	  obtain ⟨V, hV, hxV, hD⟩ :=
187	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_isDedekindDomain_section f x
188	  exact hV.specializes_eq_genericPoint_or_eq hD hxV h
189	
190	/-- **Existence of a transcendental rational function.**  On an integral scheme smooth of
191	relative dimension `1` over a field `K`, the function field contains an element `f₀`
192	transcendental over `K`, where `K` acts on the function field through the structure morphism
193	(global sections followed by the germ at the generic point).
194	
195	The element is the étale coordinate of a standard smooth chart
196	(`Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_transcendental`). -/
197	theorem SmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_transcendental_functionField
198	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f] [IsIntegral X] :
199	    ∃ f₀ : X.functionField, ∀ P : Polynomial K, P ≠ 0 →
200	      Polynomial.eval₂ ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).inv ≫ f.appTop ≫
201	        X.presheaf.germ ⊤ (genericPoint X) trivial).hom f₀ P ≠ 0 := by
202	  classical
203	  obtain ⟨U, hU, V, hV, hxV, e, hsm⟩ :=
204	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_isStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension (n := 1) (f := f)
205	      (genericPoint X)
206	  have hUtop : U = ⊤ := by
207	    have hsub : Subsingleton (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) :=
208	      inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (PrimeSpectrum K))
209	    refine TopologicalSpace.Opens.ext (Set.eq_univ_of_forall fun y => ?_)
210	    exact Subsingleton.elim (f.base (genericPoint X)) y ▸ e hxV
211	  subst hUtop
212	  letI : Field Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of K), ⊤) :=
213	    ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv.toMulEquiv.isField
214	      (Field.toIsField K)).toField
215	  haveI : Nonempty V := ⟨⟨genericPoint X, hxV⟩⟩
216	  algebraize [(f.appLE ⊤ V e).hom]
217	  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_transcendental
218	    Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of K), ⊤) Γ(X, V)
219	  refine ⟨(X.presheaf.germ V (genericPoint X) hxV).hom t, fun P hP => ?_⟩
220	  -- Rewrite the structure composite through the chart.
221	  have hcomp : (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).inv ≫ f.appTop ≫
222	      X.presheaf.germ ⊤ (genericPoint X) trivial =
223	      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).inv ≫ f.appLE ⊤ V e ≫
224	        X.presheaf.germ V (genericPoint X) hxV := by
225	    simp only [Scheme.Hom.appLE, Category.assoc]
226	    rw [X.presheaf.germ_res (homOfLE e) _ hxV]
227	    rfl
228	  rw [hcomp]
229	  -- Unfold the composite evaluation into a germ of an `aeval` in the chart.
230	  have heval : Polynomial.eval₂ ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).inv ≫ f.appLE ⊤ V e ≫
231	      X.presheaf.germ V (genericPoint X) hxV).hom
232	        ((X.presheaf.germ V (genericPoint X) hxV).hom t) P =
233	      (X.presheaf.germ V (genericPoint X) hxV).hom
234	        (Polynomial.aeval t (P.map (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).inv.hom)) := by
235	    rw [Polynomial.aeval_def, RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra, Polynomial.hom_eval₂,
236	      Polynomial.eval₂_map]
237	    rfl
238	  rw [heval]
239	  -- The germ map is injective on the integral scheme `X`, and `t` is transcendental.
240	  intro hzero
241	  have hinj : Function.Injective ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).inv.hom : K →+* _) :=
242	    ((ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective
243	      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).inv).mp inferInstance).injective
244	  have hmap : P.map (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).inv.hom ≠ 0 :=
245	    fun h0 => hP ((Polynomial.map_eq_zero_iff hinj).mp h0)
246	  refine ht ⟨P.map (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).inv.hom, hmap, ?_⟩
247	  refine germ_injective_of_isIntegral X (genericPoint X) hxV ?_
248	  rw [map_zero]
249	  exact hzero
250	
251	end SmoothCurve

9	
10	The Jacobian challenge (`AlgebraicJacobian.Challenge`) works with a bundle
11	`C : Over (Spec (.of k))` together with the instances `[IsProper C.hom]`,
12	`[SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]` and `[GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]`.

14	as instances keyed on the `Over`-bundle:
15	
16	* `AlgebraicGeometry.irreducibleSpace_left_of_geometricallyIrreducible`:
17	  a scheme geometrically irreducible over a field is irreducible (in particular nonempty).
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.compactSpace_left_of_quasiCompact` and
19	  `AlgebraicGeometry.quasiSeparatedSpace_left_of_quasiSeparated`:
20	  a scheme quasi-compact (resp. quasi-separated) over `Spec k` is a quasi-compact
21	  (resp. quasi-separated) topological space; both hypotheses hold for proper morphisms.
22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced`:
23	  a scheme geometrically reduced and geometrically irreducible over a field is integral.
24	  In particular Mathlib's function-field API (`Scheme.functionField`) applies to `C.left`.
25	
26	Geometric reducedness is taken as a *hypothesis* here: the implication
27	"smooth ⟹ geometrically reduced" is proved elsewhere in this project
28	(`AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.GeometricallyReduced`), never in this file.
29	
30	Statements are given for an arbitrary `X : Over (Spec (.of k))` with the minimal hypotheses,
31	so that they also apply to the Jacobian bundle itself in later waves.

7	/-!
8	# `ModuleCat k`-valued sheaf cohomology and the structure sheaf as a sheaf of modules
9	
10	This file provides the cohomology carrier for the genus lane of the Jacobian challenge:
11	
12	1. For a small site `(C, J)` and a commutative ring `R`, the degree-`n` cohomology
13	   `Sheaf.HModule F n` of a sheaf `F` of `R`-modules, defined as the `Ext`-group from the
14	   constant sheaf with value `R` to `F` (mirroring `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H`, which is
15	   `AddCommGrpCat`-valued; ours is `ModuleCat R`-valued so that `Module.finrank` applies).
16	   Each `Sheaf.HModule F n` is an `R`-module via the `R`-linear structure of the sheaf
17	   category, and `Sheaf.HModule.map` gives `R`-linear functoriality in `F`.
18	2. The degree-zero identification `Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀ : HModule F 0 ≃ₗ[R] F(⊤)`
19	   via `Ext⁰ ≅ Hom` and the constant-sheaf adjunction, together with its naturality.
20	3. For a scheme `X` over `Spec k`, the structure sheaf of `X` as a sheaf of `k`-modules
21	   `Scheme.moduleKSheaf` on the small Zariski site `Opens.grothendieckTopology X`, by
22	   restriction of scalars along the structure morphism, with definitional (`rfl`) access
23	   to its sections and restriction maps.
24	
25	## Universe discipline
26	
27	Everything is single-universe: `k : Type u`, `X : Scheme.{u}`, the site `Opens X : Type u`
28	with hom-types in `Type u`, and coefficients `ModuleCat.{u} k`. Then
29	`Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) (ModuleCat.{u} k)` is Grothendieck abelian relative
30	to `u` (`ModuleCat.{u} k` is, and the site is small), hence `HasExt.{u}` holds and
31	`Sheaf.HModule F n : Type u` with a `Module k` structure — no universe bump anywhere, so
32	`Module.finrank k` applies directly downstream.
33	
34	## Design notes
35	
36	* `Sheaf.HModule` is an `abbrev` for `Abelian.Ext`, so the entire mathlib `Ext` API
37	  (long exact sequences `Ext.covariant_sequence_exact₁/₂/₃`, `Ext.extClass`, the
38	  Mayer–Vietoris machinery of `CategoryTheory/Sites/SheafCohomology`) applies
39	  transparently; we do not rebuild any of it.
40	* No global `Algebra k Γ(X, U)` instance is introduced (it would overlap with mathlib's
41	  `Algebra R Γ(Spec R, U)` instance via the tautological `OverClass X X`); the module
42	  structure is carried by the explicit defs `Scheme.overAlgebraMap`/`Scheme.overModule`
43	  and, where needed, `attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule`.
44	-/

54	namespace Sheaf

60	variable (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
61	  [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} R)]
62	
63	/-- The constant sheaf of `R`-modules with value `R` on the site `(C, J)`; sheaf cohomology
64	of sheaves of `R`-modules is `Ext` out of this object. -/
65	noncomputable def constModuleSheaf : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R) :=
66	  (constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj (ModuleCat.of R R)

68	variable {J R}
69	
70	/-- The degree-`n` cohomology of a sheaf of `R`-modules on a small site, as an `Ext`-group
71	in the Grothendieck abelian category `Sheaf J (ModuleCat R)`. It is a `Type u` carrying a
72	`Module R` instance (via the `R`-linear structure of the sheaf category). -/
73	noncomputable abbrev HModule (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (n : ℕ) : Type u :=
74	  Abelian.Ext (constModuleSheaf J R) F n

80	/-- Functoriality of `Sheaf.HModule` in the sheaf, as an `R`-linear map. -/
81	noncomputable def map (f : F ⟶ G) (n : ℕ) : HModule F n →ₗ[R] HModule G n :=
82	  (Abelian.Ext.mk₀ f).postcompOfLinear R (constModuleSheaf J R) (add_zero n)

8	# Global sections of a proper geometrically integral scheme over a field
9	
10	The keystone of the curve substrate: for a scheme `X` proper and geometrically integral over a
11	field `K`, the structure map induces an isomorphism `K ≅ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`.
12	
13	* `AlgebraicGeometry.bijective_appTop_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral`:
14	  the honest general form — `f.appTop : Γ(Spec K, ⊤) ⟶ Γ(X, ⊤)` is bijective.
15	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_appTop_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral` and the bundle instance
16	  `AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_hom_appTop_of_geometricallyReduced`: the instance-friendly forms.
17

19	
20	Write `A := Γ(X, ⊤)`. By Mathlib's properness facts (`isField_of_universallyClosed`,
21	`finite_appTop_of_universallyClosed`), `A` is a field, finite over `K`. Base change `f` along
22	`Spec A ⟶ Spec K`: the total space `X_A` is again proper and geometrically integral over the
23	field `A`, so `Γ(X_A, ⊤)` is a field as well. Flat base change of sections
24	(`isIso_pushoutSection_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_flat_right`) exhibits `Γ(X_A, ⊤)` as the pushout
25	`A ⊗[K] A`. A pushout of a field extension along itself being a field forces `K ⟶ A` to be an
26	*epimorphism* of rings (`CommRingCat.epi_of_isPushout_of_isField`: the codiagonal
27	`A ⊗[K] A ⟶ A` is injective, being a ring map out of a field, and surjective, being split by
28	`inl`; hence `inl` is an isomorphism and the two coprojections agree). A finite ring
29	epimorphism is surjective (`RingHom.surjective_of_epi_of_finite`), and any ring map out of a
30	field is injective.
31

33	challenge it is supplied by "smooth ⟹ geometrically reduced", proved elsewhere in this project.
34	-/

44	/-- If a pushout square of commutative rings has isomorphic legs (`e : C ≅ B` intertwining
45	`ψ` and `φ`) and its pushout `D` is a field, then `φ` is an epimorphism.
46	
47	This is the classical "diagonal" criterion: the codiagonal `μ : D ⟶ B` determined by
48	`𝟙 B` and `e.hom` is injective (a ring map out of a field into a nontrivial ring) and split
49	surjective, hence an isomorphism; so `inl = e.inv ≫ inr`, which makes `φ` epi. -/
50	lemma epi_of_isPushout_of_isField {A B C D : CommRingCat.{u}}
51	    {φ : A ⟶ B} {ψ : A ⟶ C} {inl : B ⟶ D} {inr : C ⟶ D}
52	    (H : IsPushout φ ψ inl inr) (hD : IsField D) [Nontrivial B]
53	    (e : C ≅ B) (he : ψ ≫ e.hom = φ) : Epi φ := by
54	  letI : Field D := hD.toField
55	  -- the codiagonal
56	  let μ : D ⟶ B := H.desc (𝟙 B) e.hom (by rw [Category.comp_id, he])
57	  have hμinl : inl ≫ μ = 𝟙 B := H.inl_desc _ _ _
58	  have hμinr : inr ≫ μ = e.hom := H.inr_desc _ _ _
59	  have : IsIso μ := by
60	    refine (ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective μ).mpr ⟨μ.hom.injective, fun b ↦ ⟨inl b, ?_⟩⟩
61	    simpa using congr($(hμinl) b)
62	  -- the two coprojections agree up to `e`
63	  have key : e.inv ≫ inr = inl := by
64	    rw [← cancel_mono μ, Category.assoc, hμinr, hμinl, Iso.inv_hom_id]
65	  refine ⟨fun {W} u v huv ↦ ?_⟩
66	  have w : φ ≫ u = ψ ≫ (e.hom ≫ v) := by
67	    rw [← Category.assoc, he]; exact huv
68	  calc u = inl ≫ H.desc u (e.hom ≫ v) w := (H.inl_desc _ _ _).symm
69	    _ = e.inv ≫ inr ≫ H.desc u (e.hom ≫ v) w := by rw [← Category.assoc, key]
70	    _ = e.inv ≫ e.hom ≫ v := by rw [H.inr_desc]
71	    _ = v := by rw [Iso.inv_hom_id_assoc]

/-!
# Adic valuations on Dedekind domains
Given a Dedekind domain `R` of Krull dimension 1 and a maximal ideal `v` of `R`, we define the
`v`-adic valuation on `R` and its extension to the field of fractions `K` of `R`.
We prove several properties of this valuation, including the existence of uniformizers.

We define the completion of `K` with respect to the `v`-adic valuation, denoted
`v.adicCompletion`, and its ring of integers, denoted `v.adicCompletionIntegers`.

## Main definitions
- `IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.intValuation v` is the `v`-adic valuation on `R`.
- `IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.valuation v` is the `v`-adic valuation on `K`.
- `IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.adicCompletion v` is the completion of `K` with respect
  to its `v`-adic valuation.
- `IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.adicCompletionIntegers v` is the ring of integers of
  `v.adicCompletion`.
- `IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.adicAbv v` is the `v`-adic absolute value on `K` defined as
  `b` raised to negative `v`-adic valuation, for some `b` in `ℝ≥0`.

## Main results
- `IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.intValuation_le_one` : The `v`-adic valuation on `R` is
  bounded above by 1.
- `IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.intValuation_lt_one_iff_dvd` : The `v`-adic valuation of
  `r : R` is less than 1 if and only if `v` divides the ideal `(r)`.
- `IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.intValuation_le_pow_iff_dvd` : The `v`-adic valuation of
  `r : R` is less than or equal to `WithZero.exp (-n)` if and only if `vⁿ` divides the
  ideal `(r)`.
- `IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.intValuation_exists_uniformizer` : There exists `π : R`
  with `v`-adic valuation `WithZero.exp (-1)`.
- `IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.valuation_of_mk'` : The `v`-adic valuation of `r / s : K`
  is the valuation of `r` divided by the valuation of `s`.
- `IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.valuation_of_algebraMap` : The `v`-adic valuation on `K`
  extends the `v`-adic valuation on `R`.
- `IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.valuation_exists_uniformizer` : There exists `π : K` with
  `v`-adic valuation `WithZero.exp (-1)`.

## Implementation notes
We are only interested in Dedekind domains with Krull dimension 1.

## References
* [G. J. Janusz, *Algebraic Number Fields*][janusz1996]
* [J.W.S. Cassels, A. Fröhlich, *Algebraic Number Theory*][cassels1967algebraic]
* [J. Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*][Neukirch1992]

## Tags

/-! ### Adic valuations on the field of fractions `K` -/

variable (K) in
/-- The `v`-adic valuation of `x : K` is the valuation of `r` divided by the valuation of `s`,
where `r` and `s` are chosen so that `x = r/s`. -/
def valuation (v : HeightOneSpectrum R) : Valuation K ℤᵐ⁰ :=
  v.intValuation.extendToLocalization
    (fun r hr => Set.mem_compl <| v.intValuation_ne_zero' ⟨r, hr⟩) K

theorem valuation_def (x : K) :
    v.valuation K x =
      v.intValuation.extendToLocalization
        (fun r hr => Set.mem_compl (v.intValuation_ne_zero' ⟨r, hr⟩)) K x :=
  rfl

/--
The `v`-adic valuation of `r / s : K` is the valuation of `r` divided by the valuation of `s`. -/
theorem valuation_of_mk' {r : R} {s : nonZeroDivisors R} :
    v.valuation K (IsLocalization.mk' K r s) = v.intValuation r / v.intValuation s := by
  rw [valuation_def, Valuation.extendToLocalization_mk', div_eq_mul_inv]

open scoped algebraMap in
/-- The `v`-adic valuation on `K` extends the `v`-adic valuation on `R`. -/
theorem valuation_of_algebraMap (r : R) : v.valuation K r = v.intValuation r := by
  rw [valuation_def, Valuation.extendToLocalization_apply_map_apply]

open scoped algebraMap in
/-- The `v`-adic valuation on `R` is bounded above by 1. -/
theorem valuation_le_one (r : R) : v.valuation K r ≤ 1 := by
  rw [valuation_of_algebraMap]; exact v.intValuation_le_one r

/-- The `v`-adic valuation of `r : R` is less than 1 if and only if `v` divides the ideal `(r)`. -/
theorem valuation_lt_one_iff_dvd (r : R) :
    v.valuation K r < 1 ↔ v.asIdeal ∣ Ideal.span {r} := by
  rw [valuation_of_algebraMap]; exact v.intValuation_lt_one_iff_dvd r

open scoped algebraMap in
/-- The `v`-adic valuation of `r : R` is less than 1 if and only if `r ∈ v`. -/
theorem valuation_lt_one_iff_mem (r : R) :
    v.valuation K r < 1 ↔ r ∈ v.asIdeal := by
  rw [valuation_of_algebraMap]; exact v.intValuation_lt_one_iff_mem r

  rw [← HeightOneSpectrum.valuation_lt_one_iff_mem (K := K), le_antisymm_iff]

/--

protected abbrev Over (X S : Scheme.{u}) := OverClass X S

/--
`X.CanonicallyOver S` is the typeclass containing the data of a structure morphism `X ↘ S : X ⟶ S`,
and that `S` is (uniquely) inferable from the structure of `X`.
-/
abbrev CanonicallyOver (X S : Scheme.{u}) := CanonicallyOverClass X S

/-- Given `X.Over S` and `Y.Over S` and `f : X ⟶ Y`,

abbrev Hom.IsOver (f : X.Hom Y) (S : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over S] [Y.Over S] := HomIsOver f S
